comment: Single source of truth for deterministic formatter rules on every platform. The pipeline order is: trim, fillers, spoken punctuation, scratch-that, whitespace, numbers, capitalization, terminal punctuation. Spoken punctuation runs before scratch-that so sentence boundaries exist. Levels: off applies nothing but a trim; light applies fillers, whitespace, capitalization; full applies everything. Change behavior here or nowhere.

fillers.comment: Standalone filler words removed at light and full. Word-boundary, case-insensitive. Never part of another word.

scratchThat.comment: Full level: each trigger deletes the current sentence up to and including the trigger, keeping what follows. Sentence start is the position after the previous . ! ? or newline.

spokenPunctuation.comment: Full level: spoken commands become symbols. Longest phrase wins. Terminal symbols capitalize the next word. Newline commands also swallow surrounding spaces. This is a command vocabulary: speaking the word literally converts, which is the accepted tradeoff of deterministic dictation.

numbers.comment: Setting digits converts standalone number words to digits: units 0-20, tens, and tens-units pairs (with or without hyphen). Setting words converts standalone digits 0-20 to words. Setting auto leaves the transcript as the model produced it.

terminalPunctuation.comment: Full level: a transcript of three or more words that ends on a word character gets a closing period.
